title: A boundary between sensors
stem: Two sensors are at $A(-2,5)$ and $B(6,1)$. A service boundary consists of all points equidistant from them.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find a Cartesian equation of the boundary.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A straight road follows $y=8-x$. Find the point on the road equidistant from the sensors.

steps.text: Use the midpoint and perpendicular gradient.
The midpoint is $(2,3)$ and the gradient of $AB$ is $-4/8=-1/2$.
The perpendicular bisector has gradient $2$, so $y-3=2(x-2)$, or $y=2x-1$.
Solve the two line equations simultaneously.
At the crossing, $2x-1=8-x$, so $x=3$ and $y=5$. The point is $(3,5)$.

title: Two calibration scales
stem: A sensor reading $r$ depends linearly on temperature $T$ in °C. Readings of 14 and 50 correspond to 5 °C and 25 °C respectively.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $r$ as a function of $T$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the inverse rule. If a displayed reading of 32 was rounded to the nearest integer, give the interval of possible temperatures. Take half-integers to round up.

steps.text: Find the change in reading per degree.
Using the first reading gives $14=9+ c$, so $r=9T/5+5$.
Invert the linear rule and convert both rounding limits.
$T=5(r-5)/9$. The unrounded reading satisfies $31.5\le r<32.5$.
The scale is increasing, so $265/18\le T<275/18$ °C.

title: A triangle cut by a line
stem: A straight line of negative gradient passes through $(2,3)$ and meets the positive coordinate axes at $(a,0)$ and $(0,b)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that $b=3a/(a-2)$ and state the possible values of $a$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The coordinate axes and the line enclose an area of 16 square units. Find both possible equations of the line.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: As the line pivots about $(2,3)$, prove that the area cannot fall below 12 square units. Determine the line for which this bound is reached.

steps.text: Use both axis intercepts to write the line equation.
The intercept equation is $x/a+y/b=1$. Substituting $(2,3)$ gives $3/b=(a-2)/a$.
Since $a,b>0$, this requires $a>2$.
Substitute the intercept relation into the triangle area.
The intercept pairs are $(8/3,12)$ and $(8,4)$.
The lines are $9x+2y=24$ and $x+2y=8$.
Compare the area with 12 by completing a square.
The area is $A=3a^{2}/(2(a-2))$.
Subtracting 12 gives $A-12=3(a-4)^{2}/(2(a-2))\ge 0$ since $a>2$.
Equality occurs at $a=4$, giving $b=6$ and the line $3x+2y=12$.

title: A tank that starts leaking
stem: A tank is filled at a constant rate. At 2 min it contains 17.6 L; at 7 min it contains 32.1 L. At 8 min a leak starts, removing 1.35 L/min while filling continues.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the volume at the instant the leak starts.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the time, measured from the start of filling, when the volume reaches 50 L.

steps.text: Find the rate before the leak.
The filling rate is $(32.1-17.6)/5=2.90$ L/min.
One minute after the second reading the tank contains $32.1+2.90=35.0$ L.
Use the net rate after the leak starts.
After 8 min the net rate is $2.90-1.35=1.55$ L/min.
Solve $35+1.55(t-8)=50$ to obtain $t=17.7$ min.

title: Order of two linear adjustments
stem: Two machines apply the rules $f(x)=3x-4$ and $g(x)=mx+c$. The graph of $g$ passes through $(4,9)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the condition on $m$ and $c$ for both orders of processing to give the same output for every input.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Hence determine the equation of the line representing $g$ and its intersection with the graph of $f$.

steps.text: Compare the constants in the two compositions.
$f(g(x))=3mx+3c-4$ and $g(f(x))=3mx-4m+c$.
Equal constant terms give $c=2-2m$.
Use the known point as the second condition on the line.
Equating $3x-4$ and $7x/2-5$ gives $x=2$, so the lines meet at $(2,2)$.

title: A family of lines
stem: For each real $k$, let $L_k$ have equation $(k-1)x+(k+2)y=6$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that all the lines pass through one fixed point and find its coordinates.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the member perpendicular to $2x-y=7$. Also identify the vertical member of the family.

steps.text: Equate the coefficient of the parameter to zero.
Write $k(x+y)-x+2y=6$. A point on every line satisfies $x+y=0$ and $-x+2y=6$.
Use a negative reciprocal gradient; examine the vertical case separately.
The given gradient is $2$, so $-(k-1)/(k+2)=-1/2$.
This gives $k=4$ and $x+2y=2$.
The vertical case is $k=-2$, giving $x=-2$.

title: An arch from three measurements
stem: A parabolic arch meets level ground at horizontal coordinates $x=1$ and $x=9$ metres. Its height at $x=3$ is 6 m.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the height function in factorised form and determine its maximum height.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the width of the arch at a height of 4 m.

steps.text: Use the two known zeros to factor the height function.
By symmetry the maximum is $h(5)=8$ m.
Solve at the specified height and subtract the positions.
Write $h=8-(x-5)^{2}/2$. Then $(x-5)^{2}=8$ gives positions $5\pm 2\sqrt{2}$.
Their separation is $4\sqrt{2}$ m.

title: Choosing a tangent
stem: Consider the parabola $y=x^{2}-2x+5$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the gradients of the two tangents to the parabola that pass through the origin, without differentiating.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the horizontal distance between the two points of contact.

steps.text: Require a repeated intersection of the line and parabola.
A line $y=mx$ gives $x^{2}-(m+2)x+5=0$.
A repeated root needs $(m+2)^{2}=20$, hence $m=-2\pm 2\sqrt{5}$.
The vertical line through the origin is not a tangent.
Use the repeated-root formula to locate both contact points.
The repeated root is $x=(m+2)/2$, so the contact coordinates have $x=\pm \sqrt{5}$. The distance in the horizontal direction is $2\sqrt{5}$.

title: A price decision
stem: At a price of $p$ dollars, a theatre expects to sell $420-12p$ seats. Its cost for a performance is 1200 dollars plus 3 dollars per seat sold. Prices must be whole dollars with $3\le p\le 35$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Obtain a quadratic expression for the expected profit.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the price giving the greatest expected profit and all prices giving at least 1500 dollars profit.

steps.text: Subtract the variable and fixed costs from revenue.
Use the vertex for the optimum and the roots for the threshold.
The vertex is at $p=19$, an allowed integer.
For the threshold solve $p^{2}-38p+330\le 0$, with roots $19\pm \sqrt{31}$ (about 13.43 and 24.57).
Thus every integer from 14 to 24 inclusive qualifies.

title: A displaced parabola

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the length of the horizontal chord of $g$ lying 9 units above its vertex.

steps.text: Use symmetry to locate the new axis.
The axis is halfway between the zeros, at $x=3$. The leading coefficient remains 1.
Set the height relative to the vertex.
This chord has $y=-7$, so $(x-3)^{2}=9$.
Its endpoints have $x=0,6$ and its length is 6.

title: Comparing a quadratic with its input
stem: Let $f(x)=x^{2}-2ax+a+2$, where $a$ is real.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine all $a$ for which $f(x)>x$ for every real $x$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: At the larger boundary value, find the fixed point of $f$.

steps.text: Apply a strict discriminant condition to the difference.
The quadratic $f(x)-x=x^{2}-(2a+1)x+a+2$ opens upwards.
Strict positivity requires $(2a+1)^{2}-4(a+2)<0$, or $4a^{2}-7<0$.
Thus $-\sqrt{7}/2<a<\sqrt{7}/2$.
Use the repeated root at the boundary parameter.
When $a=\sqrt{7}/2$, the quadratic has a double root at $x=(2a+1)/2=(\sqrt{7}+1)/2$. This input equals its output.

title: Reading a broken-line graph
stem: The figure shows the complete graph of $f$. Adjacent marked points are joined by straight segments; a hollow endpoint is excluded.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the domain and range of $f$. Find the gradient of the segment to the right of the maximum.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find all $k$ for which $f(x)=k$ has exactly two solutions.

steps.text: Read closed and open endpoints from the graph.
The domain is $[-3,5)$; the maximum of 4 occurs at $x=1$ and the minimum of 0 at $x=-3$, so the range is $[0,4]$.
The right-hand gradient is $(2-4)/(5-1)=-1/2$.
Compare the sets of heights reached on both segments.
The increasing segment covers $[0,4]$, while the decreasing segment covers $(2,4]$. At 4 they share one point; at 2 the right endpoint is absent.
Thus $2<k<4$.

title: An excluded endpoint
stem: The function $f(x)=5-\sqrt{2x+6}$ is defined for $-3\le x<5$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find its range, taking account of the endpoint convention.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the inverse rule and its domain.

steps.text: Follow the square root from the included to the excluded endpoint.
$2x+6$ increases from 0 up to, but not including, 16.
Hence $0\le \sqrt{2x+6}<4$, giving $1<f(x)\le 5$.
Isolate the root before squaring and reversing the variables.
On this interval the square root has the required sign.

title: A domain that survives composition
stem: Let $u(x)=\sqrt{5-x}$ and $v(x)=1/(x-1)$, each on its largest real domain.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the domain of $v\circ u$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the range of $u$ on the domain you found in part (a).

steps.text: Check both the square root and the outer denominator.
The square root requires $x\le 5$. The denominator is zero when $\sqrt{5-x}=1$, i.e.
$x=4$. Thus the domain is $(-\infty ,4)\cup (4,5]$.
Determine which output corresponds to the removed input.
For $x\le 5$, the root covers $[0,\infty )$ exactly once. Removing $x=4$ removes only the value 1.
The range is $[0,1)\cup (1,\infty )$.

title: Monitoring a signal
subtopic: Key features and sketches of graphs
stem: On the interval $0\le t\le 5$, a signal has strength $S(t)=4+t(5-t)e^{-0.3t}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use graphing technology to determine the range of $S$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For how long is the strength above 7? Give your answer in the same time units as $t$.

steps.text: Find the interior maximum and compare it with the endpoint values.
Plot on $[0,5]$. The maximum tool gives its peak at $t\approx 1.667$, with $S\approx 7.3696$.
The extra term is non-negative and vanishes at both ends. The range, to three significant figures, is $[4,7.37]$.
Find both threshold crossings before subtracting their times.
Intersect the graph with $y=7$ on either side of its peak. The crossings are at $t\approx 1.02830$ and $t\approx 2.44495$.
The curve lies above 7 between them, for approximately 1.42 time units.

title: The missing output
stem: On its largest real domain let $f(x)=(3x+1)/(x-2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: By rearranging $y=f(x)$, identify the missing output and justify that every other real output occurs.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Now restrict to $x>2$. Give the new range and the equations of the two asymptotes of this branch.

steps.text: Solve the level equation for the input.
$x(y-3)=2y+1$. The choice $y=3$ gives a contradiction.
For every $y\ne 3$, $x=(2y+1)/(y-3)$ is defined and cannot be 2, since that would require $1=-6$. Only 3 is missing.
Rewrite the rule as a constant plus a reciprocal.
$f(x)=3+7/(x-2)$; the positive fraction takes every positive value.
The range is $(3,\infty )$ and the asymptotes are $x=2$ and $y=3$.

title: Fitting a shifted graph
stem: The graph of $g(x)=a\sqrt{x-h}+k$ starts at $(3,7)$ and passes through $(12,1)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine $a,h,k$ and give the domain and range.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Describe a sequence of transformations taking $y=\sqrt{x}$ to this graph.

steps.text: Use the starting point and the second given point.
The endpoint gives $h=3,k=7$. Then $1=3a+7$, so $a=-2$.
The domain is $[3,\infty )$ and the range is $(-\infty ,7]$.
Describe the output scaling and the shifts in a valid order.
Stretch vertically by factor 2, reflect in the horizontal axis, then translate 3 units right and 7 units up.
This produces $g(x)=-2\sqrt{x-3}+7$.

title: Two charging rules
stem: An order of value $x$ dollars, $x\ge 20$, receives a 15% discount $D$ and a fixed handling charge $H$ of 8 dollars.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find expressions for $(D\circ H)(x)$ and $(H\circ D)(x)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A receipt for 76 dollars applied the handling charge last. Reconstruct the original order value and find the saving if the order of the rules were reversed.

steps.text: Apply the inner operation first in each order.
Hence $(D\circ H)(x)=0.85x+6.80$ and $(H\circ D)(x)=0.85x+8$.
Undo the handling charge, then the discount.
$0.85x+8=76$ gives $x=80$ dollars.
Reversing the rules reduces the constant term by $8-6.80=1.20$ dollars, irrespective of $x$.

title: When the order changes the domain
stem: Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x-2}$ and $g(x)=x^{2}+1$, on their natural real domains.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find both composite rules and their respective domains.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether the two composite graphs intersect.

steps.text: Check the original inner-function domain in each order.
$(f\circ g)(x)=\sqrt{x^{2}-1}$ requires $x\le -1$ or $x\ge 1$.
Meanwhile $(g\circ f)(x)=x-1$, but the inner root still requires $x\ge 2$.
Work on the common domain and test the candidate root.
On the shared domain $x\ge 2$, equality requires $\sqrt{x^{2}-1}=x-1$. Squaring gives $x^{2}-1=x^{2}-2x+1$, whence $x=1$.
This is outside the shared domain, so there is no intersection.

title: Recovering a missing process
stem: For $x\ge 1$, $f(x)=2x-1$ and $(g\circ f)(x)=4x^{2}-4x+6$.

steps.text: Introduce the output of the linear function as a new input.
Every $u\ge 1$ is reached.
Select the square-root branch allowed by the restriction.
From $y=u^{2}+5$ select the positive root since $u\ge 1$.
Thus $g^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x-5}$ for $x\ge 6$.

title: Calibrating a pair of maps
stem: For $a>0$, let $f(x)=ax+b$. Applying $f$ twice takes 1 to 7 and takes 3 to 15.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine $a$ and $b$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: An input is processed three times and then reduced by 5. Find the input if the final result is 42.

steps.text: Form the twice-applied linear map.
$(f\circ f)(x)=a^{2}x+b(a+1)$. Its gradient is $(15-7)/(3-1)=4$, so $a=2$.
From $7=4+3b$ we get $b=1$.
Apply the map once more before subtracting the final adjustment.
Three applications give $2(4x+3)+1=8x+7$.
Thus $8x+7-5=42$, giving $x=5$.

title: Composing two logarithmic scales
stem: Let $f(x)=\ln  x$ and $g(x)=e^{2x}+3$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Simplify $(g\circ f)(x)$ and state its domain.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Solve $(f\circ g)(x)=\ln  12$, giving an exact answer.

steps.text: Use the inverse relation between logarithms and exponentials.
Therefore $(g\circ f)(x)=x^{2}+3$ on $(0,\infty )$; simplification does not add $x=0$ or negative inputs.

title: Two exponential terms and a parameter
stem: For real $k$, consider $4^x-k\cdot 2^x+4=0$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For such $k$, show that the sum of the two solutions for $x$ is independent of $k$.

steps.text: Require two positive and distinct values of the substituted variable.
With $u=2^x>0$, the quadratic formula gives $u=(k\pm \sqrt{k^{2}-16})/2$.
Distinct roots require $|k|>4$.
